chunk_findings.detail: `reexports` resolves every `ImportFrom` target with `resolve_(_from_target(path, node))`, which for a sub-module re-export written as `from . import <name>` (equivalently `from <pkg> import <name>` inside the package `__init__`) yields the *package itself*, because `_from_target` returns the package when `node.module is None`. Concrete case: `ddflow/api/lifecycle/__init__.py` contains `from . import wait` (a very common facade spelling, next to the named form the docstring covers). `_from_target` returns `ddflow.api.lifecycle`, `resolve_` returns `ddflow.api.lifecycle`, and `reexports` produces `{"ddflow.api.lifecycle": {"wait"}}` -- an entry claiming the package re-exports the name `wait` "from" itself. The name `wait` actually refers to the module `ddflow.api.lifecycle.wait`, so the returned mapping is wrong per its own contract ("module -> the public names it re-exports from that module") and degenerates into a self-edge. A test that reaches the change only through the facade, e.g. `from ddflow.api import lifecycle` followed by `lifecycle.wait.run()` (or `import ddflow.api.lifecycle` then `ddflow.api.lifecycle.wait.LIMIT`), gives `facade_uses` the name `wait` for `ddflow.api.lifecycle`, but `reexports` offers no module for that name, so a change under `ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py` is still not selected -- the same class of recall miss the change is meant to close. Note the direct form `from ddflow.api.lifecycle import wait` is saved by `imports()`, so the hole is only on the facade-attribute route, which is exactly the route this fix enables.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testreach.py:reexports

chunk_findings.detail:
The `exports` and `uses` tables are independent, but they are built with `if`/`elif`: a file that is a package `__init__.py` gets an `exports` entry and is then *skipped entirely* for `uses`. So `g.uses` never contains any key for an `__init__.py` file, while `_through_facade` iterates `g.importers.get(facade, ...)` — a set that routinely contains other packages' `__init__.py` files (re-exporting subpackage facades). For those files `g.uses.get(t, {})` is always `{}`, the `names & …` test is always false, and the evidence is silently dropped, even though the docstring promises exactly that evidence ("The files importing the package `facade` AND spelling a name it re-exports from `mod`").

Demonstration: let the changed module be `ddflow/api/lifecycle/_impl.py`, with `ddflow/api/lifecycle/__init__.py` doing `from ._impl import start` (so `g.exports["ddflow.api.lifecycle"]["ddflow.api.lifecycle._impl"] == {"start"}`), and let `ddflow/api/__init__.py` do `from ddflow.api.lifecycle import start`. When the walk reaches the facade `ddflow.api.lifecycle`, `_through_facade(g, "ddflow.api.lifecycle", "ddflow.api.lifecycle._impl", hops, out)` iterates `g.importers["ddflow.api.lifecycle"]`, which contains `ddflow/api/__init__.py`; that file *does* import the facade and *does* spell `start`, so by the function's own contract it is evidence — but `g.uses` was never populated for it (it ends with `__init__.py`), so `names & g.uses.get(t, {}).get(facade, set())` is empty, the file is not added to `out.files`, and any test that only imports `ddflow.api` (e.g. `tests/compat/test_surface.py`-style `from ddflow.api import start`) is still missed — the very class of facade-mediated misses this change exists to fix. The `elif` should be a second `if`, so that a package `__init__` can be both an exporter and a user.

chunk_findings.detail: `reexports` credits a `from . import X` re-export to the containing package instead of to the module the name actually comes from. `_from_target` resolves a level-1 `ImportFrom` with no module to the package itself, so for `ddflow/api/lifecycle/__init__.py` whose body is `from . import wait` (the submodule that holds the changed code), `resolve_(_from_target(...))` is `ddflow.api.lifecycle` and `reexports` returns `{"ddflow.api.lifecycle": {"wait"}}` — not `{"ddflow.api.lifecycle.wait": {"wait"}}`. The docstring's contract is "module -> the public names it re-exports **from that module**", so a consumer transposing this map into name->module (the only thing the cheaper facade rule can do with it) resolves the test's `from ddflow.api.lifecycle import wait; wait.f()` to the facade package, which the test already imports, and the changed module behind the `__init__` is still not reached — precisely the recall miss (a2979659/b45b0071) this change exists to fix. The neighbouring `_imports` handles the identical statement explicitly ("`from pkg import mod` imports the MODULE when `mod` is one") and adds `ddflow.api.lifecycle.wait`; `reexports` has no such branch, and it likewise ignores re-exports written as `import ddflow.api.lifecycle.wait as wait` (it only walks `ast.ImportFrom`), so any facade that publishes a submodule by name rather than by `from X import Y` keeps its names keyed to the wrong module.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `elif` to `if` makes every package `__init__.py` that imports a facade be recorded in `g.uses`. `g.uses` is the reverse adjacency the selector walks from a changed module back to the tests that reach it, so the walk now passes *through* facades unconditionally: with the new re-export keying, a change to `pkg/api/wait.py` marks `pkg/api/__init__.py`, then `pkg/__init__.py` (its `from pkg.api import claim` now counts because `pkg.api` is a facade), then every module that imports `pkg` — not only tests that spell the re-exported name. That is precisely the "walking through a non-hub facade" mode the intent records as rejected for cost: "Walking through a non-hub facade raised selection sizes by up to 50 tests per merge in a measured trial (a0718008 15 -> 69), so it was not enabled". The regression test cannot catch the resulting over-selection because it asserts a superset — `assert {"tests/test_sub.py", "tests/test_outer.py"} <= got, got` — unlike the neighbouring test in the same file, which asserts `got == {...}`. So a fix that inflates the selected test set (the documented failure mode) still passes this test, and the selection now emits reachable facade packages as part of the affected set.

data.body: Seen on fix-Beb27076db4: the first 'ddflow review --gate rubber_duck,critic' was moved to the background by the tool timeout and kept running; I started a second. Both recorded; the older run (reviewing the pre-fix tree, finished last) recorded rubber_duck/critic failed over my triaged fixes and counted as a full round (critic hit max_rounds 2). Expected: refuse or serialize a second review of the same gate while one is running, and drop a result whose reviewed sha is no longer the branch head.
data.title: Two concurrent ddflow review runs on one gate race: a stale run overwrote the record and burned a review round

data.claim: run_command_gate re-reads Config.load(worktree), which lacks the git-ignored local layer, so local scrub_env is ignored
data.falsifier: KEEPME stays hidden from the gate without the fix
data.mechanism: cfg not passed at the two api call sites
data.probe_output: failed before (tail [unset|unset|x]), passes after passing cfg=cfg
data.question: Does a worktree gate run miss the local config layer?

evidence.note: cfg=cfg at both run_command_gate calls in api/gates.py

chunk_findings.detail: The new test's only assertion is `"|unset]" in json.loads(out)["evidence"]["tail"]`, which does not name `KEEPME`. The scrub machinery demonstrably strips `DDFLOW_AGENT` under the *default* spec — the sibling test in this same file (`test_child_env_leaves_everything_else`: `child_env(None, {"A": "1", "DDFLOW_AGENT": "x"}) == {"A": "1"}`) pins exactly that — and `DDFLOW_AGENT` is the marker ddflow sets for its own runs, so it is present in the gate's environment and will be printed with the same `|unset]` sentinel whether or not the local layer is honoured. So on the pre-fix code the gate still strips `DDFLOW_AGENT` (default spec, since the item worktree lacks `.ddflow/local/config.toml`) and the substring `|unset]` still appears; the test is satisfied by the leak case it is supposed to catch (`KEEPME` surviving). It must assert the KEEPME-specific marker (e.g. `"KEEPME=|unset]"`) to distinguish "the local `scrub_env` reached the gate" from `DDFLOW_AGENT` being scrubbed by default. As written the change's sole verification passes on both the fixed and the unfixed code.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_env_scrub.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: The stated intent is to pass `cfg=cfg` "at the two run_command_gate calls in ddflow/api/gates.py (and the ci call site)", but the diff (part 1 of 1) contains only the two `G.run_command_gate` call sites in the main gate/rerun path — there is no hunk touching a CI gate-run call. The promised `[ci].keep_env` path is therefore still resolving its config from the worktree and the machine-local layer still does not reach the CI gate run, so the change leaves half of the bug it claims to close open. Either the CI call site is missing from this diff or the intent overstates what was done.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates.py (ci call site)
